items.title: Looking for #womenshealth information on Instagram? 4 out of 10 posts are ads
items.summary: A woman in her 40s scrolls through Instagram. Between photos of friends, recipes and vacation photos, she comes across a video about perimenopause. The woman on screen explains that perimenopause is to blame for feeling tired, having trouble remembering things, struggling to sleep or gaining weight.

items.summary: Earwigs, small, elongated insects with distinctive pincers at the rear of their abdomens, have little reason to enter open water. items.summary: Peanut allergy is one of the most serious food allergies and can lead to sudden, life-threatening reactions. items.title: Japansko selo tvrdi da se u njemu nalazi Isusov grob. Mještani ga čuvaju desetljećima
items.summary: U JAPANSKOM selu Shingo postoji legenda o Kristovom grobu. Iako je riječ o folkloru, selo ga njeguje kroz godišnji festival, čuvajući tradiciju i privlačeći znatiželjnike bez vjerskih pretenzija.

items.title: Sparse layers of 10-nanometer silver particles boost CO production from CO₂
items.summary: Electrolysis can reduce CO2 to CO, a raw material for chemical products such as fuels. Within the GreenQUEST project, an international team led by HZB chemist Prashanth Menezes has systematically investigated catalyst layers made of silver nanoparticles, varying both particle size and density.

items.summary: When a spacecraft reenters Earth's atmosphere at hypersonic velocities, its protective heat shield faces extreme conditions, including temperatures beyond 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit (1,650 degrees Celsius). items.summary: A new analysis suggests mammograms may lead to far less breast cancer overdiagnosis than some earlier studies indicated. items.summary: A team of INRAE scientists, in collaboration with Université Côte d'Azur and Nanjing Agricultural University in China, has used an innovative AI-based method to identify the sex pheromone of the lily moth1 and the olfactory receptors associated with it. items.title: That fresh cleaning smell could be filling your home with nanoparticles
items.summary: Researchers found that scented cleaners can react with ozone indoors to create billions or trillions of invisible nanoparticles that can penetrate deep into the lungs. items.title: Više od 70% obale SAD-a tone. Milijunima ljudi raste rizik od poplava
items.summary: NOVO istraživanje otkriva da više od 70% obale SAD-a tone zbog prirodnih i ljudskih faktora. Ovaj fenomen, poznat kao supsidencija, povećava rizik od poplava za milijune ljudi i infrastrukturu.

items.title: Scientists may have misread a 2-billion-year-old clue about Earth
items.summary: Scientists have found that a famous 2-billion-year-old chemical signature, once thought to record a massive global change in Earth’s carbon cycle, may instead have been produced by local magma, hydrocarbons, and methane-eating microbes. items.title: Scientists burned their own scrolls to unlock a 2,000-year-old mystery
items.summary: Scientists discovered that tiny amounts of lead in ancient ink can make writing inside burned papyrus scrolls stand out dramatically in X-ray scans. The technique could help unlock lost Greek and Roman texts preserved by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius nearly 2,000 years ago.

items.title: Quantum computer simulates matter “popping into existence”
items.summary: Scientists recreated a particle-forming process linked to the extreme physics of the early universe using a 13-ion quantum simulator. The breakthrough suggests quantum computers could eventually help researchers investigate how matter formed and evolved after the Big Bang.

items.title: Lead isotopes trace Malawi's mysterious copper ingot hoard to Congo's Kipushi mine
items.summary: In 1967, a Malawian farmer stumbled upon a hidden hoard of eight copper ingots buried beneath a tree. Now, more than half a century later, scientists have traced the metal to its source: a copper mine nearly 800 km (500 miles) away.

items.title: Two astronauts who flew farther than anyone before are taking new NASA roles
items.summary: Artemis II astronauts Victor Glover and Reid Wiseman are transitioning to emeritus status at NASA after their historic journey around the Moon earlier this year. items.title: Zepbound and Mounjaro may turn on the body’s calorie-burning brown fat
items.summary: Tirzepatide, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, activated calorie-burning brown fat in obese mice, revealing a potential metabolic effect beyond appetite suppression. If confirmed in humans, the finding could help explain the drug’s powerful benefits and inspire more comprehensive treatments for obesity

items.summary: A new study from Ben-Gurion University of the Negev (BGU) has identified a molecular switch that controls whether stressed human cells activate a survival mechanism or trigger programmed cell death (apoptosis). items.summary: A research team from The Education University of Hong Kong (EdUHK) and East China Normal University (ECNU) has published a meta-analysis demonstrating the impact of digital textbooks (DTs) on student motivation. items.summary: Scientists discovered a surprising energy paradox in the brain during REM sleep, the stage most closely associated with dreaming. items.title: Millions in the US Northeast brace for a powerful storm
items.summary: More than 40 million people in the northeastern United States braced Friday for heavy rain and strong winds as an unusually powerful storm for the season was forecast to crash into the region.

items.title: Canals full, roads submerged as Bangkok declares flood disaster
items.summary: Bangkok authorities declared a flood disaster across the Thai capital on Saturday after almost 48 hours of heavy rain left canals full, roads submerged and residents wading through deep water.

items.title: Indonesia fires threaten critically endangered orangutan: IUCN
items.summary: Wildfires that tore through Indonesian Borneo's vast tropical forests have increased pressure on critically endangered Bornean orangutans, the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) said Saturday.

items.title: Guatemala ensures survival of vulnerable 'fossil' fish
items.summary: In a freshwater canal surrounded by mangroves in southern Guatemala, hundreds of baby tropical gars—a torpedo-shaped fish with an alligator-like snout dubbed the "fossil fish"—are released into the wild.

items.title: A 'library' of bacteria-killing viruses: Harnessing the power of phages
items.summary: An estimated 38 trillion bacteria live in the human body—and only a small fraction are harmful to our health. However, the harmful ones can cause serious illness, especially when they develop resistance to antibiotics.

items.title: The secret to growing food on Mars could be fungi
items.summary: Scientists think beneficial fungi could help transform nutrient-poor lunar and Martian regolith into a material capable of supporting crops. By helping plants access nutrients and withstand harsh conditions, these microbes could someday make self-sustaining space farming more realistic.

items.title: Don’t toss cannabis leaves: They may contain rare compounds with medical potential
items.summary: Scientists discovered rare flavoalkaloids in Cannabis leaves for the first time, along with dozens of other phenolic compounds that had never been reported in the plant. items.title: Climate crisis is affecting children's nutrition
items.summary: Wildfires, floods and other extreme weather events are no longer the only ways climate change affects children around the world. Increasingly, it also affects their diets. items.summary: During a news conference at 3 p.m. EDT on Monday, Sept. 28, NASA and Boeing leadership will discuss Starliner’s development and plans for regular crew flights to and from the International Space Station.
